reasoning: The ceasefire was announced in May 2025 after intense US bombing. Historical precedent shows Houthi ceasefires are fragile - they've broken multiple agreements before. Key risk factors: 1) Houthis may resume Red Sea shipping attacks which could trigger US response, 2) Regional tensions with Israel/Iran could escalate, 3) No clear enforcement mechanism mentioned, 4) Houthis have ideological motivations beyond immediate conflict. However, both sides have incentives to maintain peace short-term. Given ~7 months until June 2026 and Houthi track record, I estimate moderate-high probability of breakdown.
